sources.note: Shumashti appears only in the Indo-Aryan language index (Dardic > Kunar: Dameli, Gawar-Bati, Grangali, Shumashti, p. 553); no StressTyp extract for it.

sources.citation: Edelman, D. I. 1983. The Dardic and Nuristani Languages (Languages of Asia and Africa). Moscow: Nauka. [English version of Edelman 1965 Dardskie jazyki]; Shumashti section pp. 167-174 '[Morgenstierne]'
sources.note: Shumashti 'Phonetics' (p. 167) lists vowels, absence of a length opposition, nasalization, diphthongs and consonants only; nothing on stress (page scan checked by eye). Family-level remark p. 43: 'Stress varies considerably from language to language. Whereas in some languages (for instance, Dameli and Shina) the stress is tending to the word-final syllables, in Kashmiri it occurs at the word-initial ones (in nouns), in Kati the stress is mobile. Sometimes it is impossible to establish a definite pattern, taking into account to what extent the respective languages have been studied.' Shumashti…

sources.citation: [Strand, Richard F. 1973. Notes on the Nuristani and Dardic languages. JAOS 93(3): 297-305] (identification from scanned content of the archive.org item 'notes-on-the-nuristani-and-dardic-language')
sources.note: Classification paper, scanned badly garbled; nothing on Shumashti stress.

sources.citation: Morgenstierne, Georg. 1950. Notes on Gawar-Bati. Skrifter utgitt av Det Norske Videnskaps-Akademi i Oslo, II. Hist.-Filos. Klasse 1950 No. 1. Oslo: Dybwad.
sources.note: Sister language Gawar-Bati (gawa1247), not Shumashti: sect. 7 'No relevant tones were observed. There is great confusion of stress.. and it is not possible to lay down any rules regarding its place.' Cites his 1945 Shumashti description (NTS 13: 239-81) but gives no Shumashti stress statement.

sources.note: The only primary description of the language (43 pp., phonology + morphology + text + vocabulary from a 1929 informant); every later treatment (Edelman 1965/1983, Bashir 2003, Fussman 1972) derives from it. Note: nb.no full-text index shows no 'stress'/'accent' tokens within its pages, so it may contain only accent marks on forms rather than a rule; needs eyes on pp. 239-250.
